definitions.meaning: A charged particle formed when an atom loses electrons (positive ion) or gains electrons (negative ion).
The attraction between oppositely charged ions, formed when one atom transfers outer electrons to another.
A giant regular repeating pattern of particles. In an ionic compound every ion is surrounded by oppositely charged ions, with no separate molecules.
A bond formed when two atoms share a pair of electrons, each atom counting the shared pair in its outer shell.
A small separate particle of joined atoms held by covalent bonds, such as a water molecule. Ionic compounds do not form molecules.
The attraction between a lattice of positive metal ions and the sea of free electrons moving around them.
Outer electrons that have left their own atoms and are free to move through a whole structure, as in a metal.
The pull between opposite charges. It holds ions together in an ionic lattice and holds metal ions in their electron sea.

mechanismSteps: Ionic bonding: sodium gives an electron away - sodium (2,8,1) transfers its lone outer electron to chlorine (2,8,7), forming a positive sodium ion and a negative chloride ion that attract each other.
The ionic lattice - the ions pack into one giant repeating lattice, every sodium ion surrounded by chloride ions; NaCl is the 1 to 1 ratio, not a molecule.
Covalent bonding: sharing, not giving - two chlorine atoms each contribute one electron to a shared pair, so both count eight outer electrons and form a molecule.
Metallic bonding: a sea of electrons - metal atoms release their outer electrons into a free-moving sea around a lattice of positive ions, which is why metals conduct and bend.
Check the thinking - a tidy formula does not mean a molecule: ask what the outer electrons do - transferred is ionic, shared is covalent, pooled is metallic.
objectives: Describe ionic bonding as electron transfer forming a giant lattice of ions
Describe covalent bonding as shared pairs of electrons forming molecules
Describe metallic bonding as positive ions in a sea of free electrons
subject: science
title: Chemical bonding: ionic, covalent, metallic

trap.explanation: The slip: The formula NaCl looks like one joined unit, like the formulas of real molecules. The fix: Salt is a giant ionic lattice: NaCl just gives the ratio, there are no separate NaCl molecules. In class, draw one corner of the lattice and ask students to circle a single NaCl molecule - they cannot, because each ion belongs to the whole pattern, not to one partner.
trap.misconception: Table salt is made of NaCl molecules.

workedExample: Build sodium chloride step by step. Step 1 (s1): sodium (2,8,1) has one outer electron and chlorine (2,8,7) needs one, so the electron transfers: sodium forms a positive sodium ion with arrangement 2,8 and chlorine forms a negative chloride ion with arrangement 2,8,8. Step 2 (s2): the ions attract each other in every direction and lock into a giant lattice where the ions alternate, so the ratio is one sodium to one chloride and the formula is NaCl. Check the count: every sodium ion is surrounded by chloride ions and the pattern never breaks into pairs - that is the sign of a lattice, not molecules.
